claims.text: A supersaturated solid solution in a non-equilibrium Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy preferentially decomposes during service or post-processing.
During decomposition, Mg segregates into discrete Mg-rich intermetallic compounds.
The transformation changes the local elemental distribution.
The transformation changes the composition of the high-temperature oxide scale.
Changes in phase constitution and oxide-scale composition alter corrosion behavior and oxidation kinetics relative to the as-cast state.
The proposed initial alloy has a supersaturated solid solution mixed with metastable intermetallic compounds.
The proposed alloy has a density below 6 g/cm³.
Controlled heat treatment will promote formation of equilibrium phases.
Controlled heat treatment will homogenize the Mg distribution.
Growth of Mg-rich intermetallic phases alters oxide-scale continuity, composition, and protective quality.
The metastable as-cast microstructure permits Mg segregation during exposure.
Localized Mg segregation promotes formation of nonuniform oxide films.
The nonuniform oxide films may be less adherent or less protective.
Localized segregation may promote galvanic effects.
The segregation-associated surface state accelerates corrosive attack and modifies oxidation kinetics.
Heat treatment toward equilibrium stabilizes the microstructure.
The stabilized microstructure produces a more uniform and adherent oxide scale.
A more uniform and adherent oxide scale retards corrosion and oxidation.
Relative to the as-cast alloy, the heat-treated alloy will have a more continuous and uniform oxide layer and a lower corrosion rate.
Relative to the as-cast alloy, the heat-treated alloy will exhibit slower high-temperature oxidation kinetics.

contradictions.description: The heat treatment is said to homogenize Mg distribution, while the proposed transformation is explicitly described as Mg segregation and growth of discrete Mg-rich phases. These could coexist at different length scales, but no such distinction is stated, leaving the proposed mediator internally ambiguous.
